instrument: Two instruments, both applying the mutant to dist/lib/evidence.js and reading runward's own output; no verdict here comes from reading the code (ADR-0046 decision 3). (1) scripts/mutation-probe.mjs as shipped, `--strict` confirmed in gateArgs, one run per function — ledgers rw/reports/mutation/probe-<fn>.jsonl. (2) A wider battery (tools/instruct.mjs in the worktree) because the shipped probe runs only `check --strict --json` and three of these four functions are NOT on that path: collectSealableEvidence and renderEvidenceLock are reached only by `check --freeze`, and collectSealableEvidence also by `check --attest` (missionStateDigest, ADR-0055); sha256's catch is reached only on a file the process cannot open. The battery is 31 observations per mutant — `check --strict --json` on all 21 missions, `check --strict` (plain text, NO_COLOR) on four of them, `check --strict --attest` on three, and `check --strict --freeze` on two (fresh copy each time, comparing the BYTES of the evidence-lock.json the run wrote). A mutant is 'identical' only when all 31 observations are byte-identical to the pristine battery.
probeMissions: BASE, common to every mission below: `node dist/cli.js init --yes --example` (runward 0.36.0, the request-triage reference mission) into an empty directory, which is green under `check --strict` (measured: exit 0). Then `node dist/cli.js check --strict --freeze` on it, which seals 18 evidence files into runward/evidence-lock.json — 11 files the manifests cite as applied evidence plus the 5 gated manifests and 2 more cited documents. That sealed tree is `m/seal`: exit 0, seal present, count 18, 0 violations. Every tampered mission is a full copy of it with exactly one thing changed. Builders kept at tools/make-missions.mjs, tools/make-freeze-missions.mjs, tools/make-extra-missions.mjs, tools/make-lock-shapes.mjs.

WRITE-SIDE missions (`check --freeze` and `check --attest`), each an unsealed copy of the base tree: f-plain, which freezes to exactly the 18-file lock, 2022 bytes, keys sorted, trailing newline present. f-bracket, which adds two house rules whose ids separate the three anchorings of `/^\[.*\]$/` — `a[b]` (contains `[`, ends with `]`, does NOT start with `[`) and `[a]b` (starts with `[`, contains `]`, does NOT end with `]`) — each `impact: LOW` so corpus divergence does not report them (an unwritten rule is only 'extra' at CRITICAL/HIGH on a gated phase), each with an `applied` row appended to the RULE CONFORMANCE table of runward/floor.md citing a file nothing else in the mission cites (code/probe-ab.ts, code/probe-ba.ts). Pristine: exit 0, `sealed 20 evidence file(s)`, both probe files in the lock. A first attempt appended the rows below the wrong table and sealed 18, which is why the row position is part of the recipe. f-unreadable was built and DISCARDED: a cited unreadable file reddens the gate with 8 EACCES conformance gaps, and `--freeze` refuses a red gate, so the write side cannot be reached that way — hence t-attest-unreadable instead.

TAMPERED (each measured on a PRISTINE tree first, so the refusal is the mission's and not a mutant's): t-file-modified (a sealed evidence file appended to after sealing) exit 1, 1 violation 'sealed evidence changed'; t-manifest-rewritten (an `applied` row in runward/floor.md rewritten to `n/a`, the RWD-2026-0008 shape) exit 1; t-manifest-touched (floor.md edited in a way that leaves everything else green, so the seal is the ONLY thing that can notice) exit 1; t-wrong-hash (one hash in the lock replaced by 64 zeros) exit 1; t-unknown-version (`version: 999`) exit 1, 'declares version 999'; t-zero-files (`files: {}`) exit 1, 'seals zero files'; t-corrupt-lock (`{ this is not json`) exit 1, 'is not valid JSON'; t-missing-file (a sealed file deleted) exit 1, 'sealed evidence missing'; t-escape-abs (`/etc/hosts` added as a lock key) and t-escape-dotdot (`../outside-secret.txt`, with that file created outside the project) both exit 1, 'sealed path escapes the project'; t-root-key (lock key `.`, which resolves EXACTLY to the project root — the only input that separates `abs === rootAbs` from `abs.startsWith(rootAbs + sep)`) exit 1, 'sealed evidence missing: .'; t-multi (version 42 + a wrong hash + an absolute key + a missing file, so all four message paths run in one process) exit 1, 4 violations; t-unreadable (a sealed, cited file chmod 000) exit 1; t-no-lock and t-lock-deleted-and-tampered (lock removed) exit 0 — the seal is opt-in, which is the control that proves the other missions' exit 1 comes from the seal.
sideFindings: The shipped probe cannot reach three of these four functions. `scripts/mutation-probe.mjs` runs only `check --strict --json`, and `collectSealableEvidence` / `renderEvidenceLock` are called from `check --freeze` and `check --attest`. Measured on the same missions: the probe reports 0/5 observable for collectSealableEvidence on f-bracket and 0/1 for renderEvidenceLock on f-plain, while the battery with `--freeze` and `--attest` reports 3/5 and 1/1. A '0/N' from the probe on a write-side function is 'the instrument does not reach here', never 'harmless'.

PRE-EXISTING, not a mutant: a lock entry naming a file the process CANNOT READ passes the seal. sha256 returns the sentinel `"unreadable"` at seal time AND at verify time, so `"path": "unreadable"` in a lock is self-satisfying. Mission t-lock-sentinel, pristine 0.36.0 build: exit 0, `✓ seal intact — 19 evidence file(s), sealed 2026-08-20`, over a chmod-000 file. That is the RWD-2026-0008 shape again — the seal reads intact over something nothing opened. It is also why the L632 mutant is measurable: it moves the sentinel and the whole verdict moves with it.

PRE-EXISTING, not a mutant: deleting runward/evidence-lock.json launders a tampered mission. Mission t-lock-deleted-and-tampered (a sealed evidence file modified, then the lock removed) is exit 0 / clean on a pristine tree, where the same tamper with the lock in place is exit 1. The seal is opt-in by construction and the code says so, but the shape is the one ADR-0045 class 1 closed for the rule corpus by counting 'unrecorded' as a gap: one file the audited party owns turns a refusal into a pass.

verdicts.evidence: FALSE GREEN, measured end to end. Shipped probe on f-bracket: no observable difference — because `check --strict --json` never calls this function. Battery: observable on 2 (freeze:f-bracket, attest:f-bracket). Close-up (tools/one.mjs, `--mode freeze --mission f-bracket`): pristine `✓ sealed 20 evidence file(s)`, mutant `✓ sealed 19 evidence file(s)` with exit 0 in BOTH runs — the run that drops a file still reports success. The file dropped is code/probe-ab.ts, cited `applied` by the rule `a[b]`, which the mutant's unanchored `/\[.*\]$/` now matches and skips as a template placeholder. Downstream (tools/regex-downstream.mjs): seal f-bracket with the mutant, restore the PRISTINE build, then modify code/probe-ab.ts — `check --strict` returns exit 0, `{present:true,count:19,violations:0}`. The same tamper against a pristine seal returns exit 1, `{count:20,violations:1}`. A mission sealed by this build reports `seal intact` over evidence that changed after sealing: the RWD-2026-0008 shape, reopened on the write side.

The mirror image, same measurement. Battery: observable on 2 (freeze:f-bracket, attest:f-bracket). Close-up: pristine `✓ sealed 20 evidence file(s)`, mutant `✓ sealed 19`, exit 0 both times; the file dropped is code/probe-ba.ts, cited by the rule `[a]b`, which the mutant's `/^\[.*\]/` now matches. Downstream (tools/regex-downstream.mjs): mutant-sealed mission, pristine build, code/probe-ba.ts modified after sealing → exit 0, `{count:19,violations:0}`, versus exit 1 / `{count:20,violations:1}` for the pristine seal. Same false green, opposite anchor.

The replacement is the visible string `"Stryker was here!"`, so if the value ever reached an artifact it would be unmissable. Battery: IDENTICAL on all 31 observations, including both `--freeze` runs (compared on the BYTES of the lock the run wrote: 2022 bytes on f-plain and 2206 on f-bracket, byte-identical to pristine) and all three `--attest` runs (the in-toto subject digest is unchanged). Direct check: froze f-bracket under this mutant and grepped the 20 lock rows for 'Stryker' — 0 occurrences. The same battery DOES see this function move (it caught 3 of the 5 mutants here), so the null reading is a measurement.
verdicts.argument: `files` is a Map used as an ORDERED SET: the mutated literal is the placeholder VALUE passed to `files.set(key, ...)`, and the map is read exactly once, as `[...files.keys()]`. Every value that leaves the function is recomputed from scratch on the next line — `out[rel] = sha256(join(root, rel))` — so the placeholder is overwritten before anything can observe it, and it is never even read to be overwritten. `Map.set` on an existing key also leaves that key's position unchanged, so the value cannot influence iteration order either. There is no path from this literal to the return value, to the lock, or to the attestation digest, for any mission.

verdicts.evidence: Identical measurement to the mutant above, on the second `files.set` (the sealedManifests loop). Battery: IDENTICAL on all 31 observations, both `--freeze` lock byte-comparisons and all three `--attest` digests included. Froze f-bracket under this mutant: `✓ sealed 20 evidence file(s)`, lock 2206 bytes — the same count and the same byte length as pristine, no 'Stryker' anywhere in the 20 rows.
verdicts.argument: Same construction, same argument: the literal is the placeholder value of a Map whose only read is `[...files.keys()]`, and every emitted hash is recomputed by `out[rel] = sha256(join(root, rel))`. This call site additionally re-sets keys the first loop may already have inserted (a gated manifest that is also cited evidence), and `Map.set` on an existing key changes neither the position nor anything a reader can see, since the value is never read. No mission can distinguish a value that nothing consumes.

verdicts.evidence: Battery: observable on 2 (freeze:f-plain, freeze:f-bracket), and on nothing else — notably NOT on the three `--attest` runs, because missionStateDigest re-sorts the keys before hashing. Close-up (tools/one.mjs `--mode freeze --mission f-plain`): the same 18 files with the same 18 hashes, written in TRAVERSAL order instead of sorted order — the lock now begins `code/src/core/ports/model-provider.port.ts`, `code/src/core/application/triage-request.usecase.ts`, `code/src/adapters/keyword-model.adapter.ts`, … with `AGENTS.md` in thirteenth position and the five gated manifests pushed to the end, where pristine writes `AGENTS.md` first and the manifests in alphabetical position. tools/order-downstream.mjs confirms the scope of the harm: a lock written by this mutant still REFUSES a file modified after sealing (exit 1, 1 violation), so this is artifact corruption, not a false green — the function's contract, stated in its own docstring as 'stable order, byte-idempotent on unchanged evidence', is what breaks. Nothing in the suite reddens; a lock file committed to a repository churns on every re-freeze.
